label: D1 reset gate drops sharply after a1 reached rare S2; policy toward a1 lowers
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == GO) * choice ;; (phase == D2) * choice ;; (phase == D2) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * choice
explanation: Raw reset gate r of unit 38 (high ~0.9 by default, falls late in episodes). Beyond timing, the dominant driver is at D1 after an a1 trial that reached rare S2: strongly lowered (about -0.36 unrewarded, -0.27 rewarded, relative to other histories), with a small lift after a2 trials. At GO and D2 it tracks the model policy: lower when the policy favours a1 (choice logit), higher when favouring a2; D2 also stays lower after a1-S2-unrewarded. The policy terms use the model own logit (internal, observable), no future variables. Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.72; an observed-only version (D1 last-trial indicators, prev/current action, reward x episode-decile interactions) scores 0.65 test. Remaining misses: late-episode windows where the unit is much lower than predicted after unrewarded a1 trials. Ceiling all 0.84.

issues: The claimed terms reproduce exactly: test R^2 beyond timing is 0.7087. The weights are -0.355 (D1 a1-S2-u), -0.269 (D1 a1-S2-r), +0.041 (D1 prev a2) and -0.088 (D2 a1-S2-u). The main claim holds: the profile's D1 residuals are a1 S2 u -0.46 and a1 S2 r -0.30, while every other previous-trial pattern stays within about 0.15.

The policy-logit terms carry real weight. The terms without any choice term score 0.52 on test. Dropping only D1 choice gives 0.64, and dropping the GO/D2 choice terms gives 0.60. The choice terms alone score 0.49.

'After a2 trials the gate rises slightly' is not robust. If (phase == D1) * value is added, the (phase == D1)*(prev_action == 2) weight flips from +0.041 to -0.042 and test R^2 rises to 0.755. Also, the a2 rise is really an a2-reached-S1 (rare) effect (residuals +0.13 and +0.145, against a2 S2 u -0.013). Splitting the term by state gives weights of 0.073 for a2->S1 and 0.032 for a2->S2. The label does not mention this mirror effect.

'Drops more if unrewarded (-0.36 vs -0.27)' depends on which other terms are in the fit. With D1 value plus (phase == D1)*(prev_reward == 0)*choice added, both a1-S2 weights become -0.316 (test 0.769).

Misses on the claimed terms show no large error by phase x previous trial. The largest are D1 after a1 S1 r (+0.094) and after a2 S1 r (+0.079), and D1 after a2 S2 u (-0.067). The worst windows are late-episode (t>=90): runs of a1 where GO/D2 are about 0.2 too high and D1 is up to 0.45 too high. Some of those D1 misses fall on window-first trials where last_is is undefined ('?'). The explanation admits these late-episode misses. Interactions with episode time (exp(ep_trial/12) x choice or x unrewarded) add at most 0.02, so the gap is not easily closed.
Overall the description holds but is incomplete. It reaches 0.71 against the 0.84 ceiling. A better 8-term set (below) reaches 0.769 and still leaves the late-episode gap.
